title: Selecting each result type opens the right record
refs: SV-9160 (INV-46; V1 baseline 55767168; Part opened the CATALOGUE part in V1)
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header click the Search box (it is a BUTTON, data-test-id global_search_trigger, not a typeable field) or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K. Global search opens as a CENTRED MODAL over the page: a text input at the top, then a scope tab strip - All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices - each showing its own result count, then results grouped by type with a count beside each heading (e.g. "Work orders (4)"). Esc closes the modal. NOTE: group headings are SENTENCE case in the build ("Work orders", "Part sales"). If a group shows nothing, click that entity's scope tab to confirm it really is 0 rather than scrolling. Modal behaviour verified on the V2 QA branch sv9160 on 14 September 2026.
1. You are signed in as a user permitted to see every record type.
2. Records exist for each type: a Work Order, a Part Sale, a Customer, an Asset, a Vendor, a STOCKED part, and a CATALOGUE-ONLY part (one that has never been stocked).
3. The seeded data covers all of these: work orders S9160-17580 to S9160-17583, customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling', its asset unit 'ZZT-4471', vendor 'ZZAUTOTEST Kestrel Parts Supply', stocked part 'ZZT-88-4412' and catalogue-only part 'ZZT-77-3300'.
custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. For each type in turn, type a term that matches a record of that type and click the row.
3. Write down which page opened each time.
4. Do this for the STOCKED part 'ZZT-88-4412'.
5. Do this for the CATALOGUE-ONLY part 'ZZT-77-3300' - search 'Vernway' if the part number returns nothing.
6. For the Asset, check the page you land on belongs to the right owning customer.
custom_expected:
1. Work Order opens the work order page. Part Sale opens the part sale page. Customer opens that customer's work-orders page. Asset opens that asset's work-orders page, for the correct owning customer. Vendor opens the vendor page.
2. A Part opens a part record you can actually use.
3. THE CATALOGUE-ONLY PART IS THE POINT OF THIS CASE. In V1 a Part result opened the CATALOGUE part page, so every part in the catalogue could be reached from search whether or not the shop had ever stocked it. If the catalogue-only part cannot be found at all, or is found but the row leads nowhere, that is a V1 capability that has gone.
IF THAT HAPPENS: mark the test Blocked, write down exactly what you searched and what the row did, and flag it - it goes to the Product Owner together with the catalogue-part question, as one decision. Do not pass this case on the grounds that opening the inventory part is what V2 intends; this suite asks only whether V1's capability survived.
Correction, 14 September 2026: an earlier version of this case was changed to require the INVENTORY part, following specification v1.3. That was wrong for a regression case - V1 is the specification this suite tests against, and V1 opened the catalogue part. The case has been put back and the difference raised as a finding instead.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the V1 behaviour recorded in the ShopView code baseline 55767168 (routingService.ts:75, which states the Part route is the CataloguePart route guard, with GlobalSearch.vue:208-235 for the navigation targets and the companyId carried for an Asset). Version 1.5 of the Global Search - Product Requirements specification (Confluence page 576978945) section 5.3 instead requires a Part row to open the inventory part - a deliberate V2 change, recorded here as a finding rather than adopted as the expectation.
Standing Rule 96 makes a V1 capability the default expectation and Standing Rule 58 makes a code-versus-document conflict a PO DECISION ITEM.
